Co. in the interim); re-entered magistracy as 3rd clk., Sept., 1872; 2nd clk., Sept., 1873; 1st clk., Feb., 1875; clk. of couns., and ch. clk., C.S.O., Feb., 1881; valuer under the "Rating Ord.", 1875, 25th June, 1881, to 19th Mar., 1883; J.P., Jan., 1882; sup. of the opium revenue, Aug., 1883, to Feb., 1885; ditto, imports and exports, June to Oct., 1887; sec. to bd. under "Taipingshan resumption ordce.", 1894-1895 (reel. thanks of govt.), sec. to insaniary properties comrn., July, 1896; ag. deputy land offr., Nov., 1894, to Jan., 1895; ditto, Mar., 1895, to Nov., 1896; dep. regisr. and appraiser, sup. ct., and comrn. for oaths, Mar., 1896; comrn. for taking acknowledgments of married women, Oct., 1896; sec. squatter's bd.; offl. recvr. in bankruptcy, Mar., 1895, to Nov., 1896; ag. asst. regisr.-gen., July to Sept., 1897; ag. regisr., sup. ct.; ag. land offr.; ag. regisr. of companies; offl. admstr., and offl. trustee, 16th Dec., 1898, to 26th Jan., 1900; mem. bd. examra., 1902; ag. regisr., sup. ct., offl. admstr., offl. trustee and regisr. of companies, 1903-04; confirmed, 1904.

SETH, G. G.—B.A., Calcutta; cadet, S.S., Nov., 1901; ag. sheriff, Singapore, Jan., 1903; passed final exam. in Malay, Jan., 1903; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, 5th Jan., 1904; ag. dep. regisr., sup. ct., Singapore, July, 1904.
SHAND, CHAS. ARTHUR.—Mem. local assembly, Antigua, 1876-1891; ditto, federal coun., 1877-1891; J.P., Antigua, 1885; mem. ex. coun., Antigua, 1887; chirrn. P.L. guardians and of several local boards, Antigua; dist. mag., Nevis, Feb., 1903; and offl. mem. leg. coun., St. Kitts-Nevis; mem. exec. coun., St. Kitts-Nevis, Oct., 1904; J.P., Nov., 1904.

SHARE, HAMNET HOLDCOTT.—Entered Royal Navy, 1880; served in H.M.S. “Tourmaline” and numerous other ships (Egypt, medal, 1882, and Khedive’s Bronze Star); sec. to Comdr.-in-Chief, Pacific station, 1899-1901; ditto, Australia station, 1901-1903; priv. sec. to gov. of N.S. Wales, May, 1903; priv. sec. to gov.-gen. of Australia, 22nd Nov., 1904.

SHARPE, SIR ALFRED, K.C.M.G. (1903), C.B. (1897).—B. 1853; H.M.’s vice-consul, Nyasaland, 14th Feb., 1891; ditto, for territories under British influence North of the Zambesi, 18th Feb., 1893; consul for same territories, 1st Feb., 1894; ag. consmr. and consul-gen. at Zomba, 7th May, 1894, to 3rd May, 1895; given rank of deputy consmr., 1st Apl., 1896; and again acted as consmr. and consul-gen., 16th Apl., 1896, to 14th July, 1897; consmr. and consul-gen., for territories under Brit. int. N. of Zambesi, 15th July, 1897; recd. Jubilee medal, 1897; consmr., commdr.-in-chief, and consul-gen., Br. Cent. Africa Prot., 1st Jan., 1902; recd. Coronation medal, 1902.

SHARPE, W. S., C.M.G. (1900).—B. 1860; capt. 4th batt. R.I. Rifles, 1893; major, Oct., 1903; inspr., Sierra Leone frontier force, Mar., 1894; 3rd consmr. to Anglo-French bdry. coman. and delimited frontier from Atlantic coast to Little Mola River, 1896; dist. consmr., Karene dist., Jan., 1897; F.R.G.S., and J.P. for the col.; transf. to N. Nigeria as asst. res., Dec., 1900; apptd. 2nd class rea., Oct., 1901.

SHAW, CAPT. BERNARD VIDAL.—Late capt. rifle brigade; priv. sec. to dir. of crim. investig., London; consmr. of pol., Capetown, 1882 to 1888 (office abolished); visiting mag., Breakwater convict station (Cape); author of “Epitome of the Criminal Law of the Cape”; sub-immigr. agt., Br. Guiana, 1889; supt. H.M.’s penal sttlmt., Massaruni, Jan., 1894; stip. mag., 1897.

SHAW, COURTENAY.—Clk. in off. of sec. to Transvaal adminstr., Mar., 1901; ag. priv. sec. to ditto, Mar. to June, 1901; priv. sec. to col. sec., Transvaal, July, 1902.

SHAWE, HENRY BENJAMIN.—Clk. at Clanwilliam, Cape Colony, 12th May, 1883; col. secy.’s off., Cape Town, Dec., 1883; sen. examnr. of accntns., 14th Apl., 1890; chief ditto, 1st July, 1894; accntn., 10th July, 1895; accntng. offr., 31st Mar., 1899; ch. clk. and acting offr., 1st Mar., 1901; ag. under col. sec., 1st Apl. to 30th Sept., 1901; asst. under col. sec., 1st Apl., 1902.

SHEA, THE HON. SIR E. D., KT. BACH. (1902).—Col. sec. and clk. of coun., Newfoundland, Jan., 1874; cashier of savings bank, and pres. of legis. coun., Feb., 1886.

SHEA, THE HON. GEORGE.—M.H.A., Ferryland (Newfdld.), 1889-93; again in 1897; mem. exec. coun. (without portfolio), 1897; mem. of treasy. bd., 1898; mayor of St. John’s, 1902; mem. exec. coun., 1904.

SHENTON, THE HON. SIR GEORGE, KT. BACH. (1893) J.P.—B. 1842; mem. of the legislature of W. Australia, 1870-74, 1875-90; on the introduction of respon. govt., col. sec. in the first ministry formed by Sir John Forrest; pres. of the legis. coun., Oct., 1892, on the death of Sir T. Campbell, Bart.; is senior mem. of the metropolitan prov.; has been mayor of Perth on eleven different occasions.

SHEPPARD, WALTER SYDNEY.—B.A., M.B., B. Ch., Cantab., civil surg. in charge of H.M.’s troops, N.E. dist., Eng., May, 1898, to May, 1899; spec. plague med. offr., India, May, 1899, to Nov., 1900; house surg., gen. hosp., Singapore, 19th Nov., 1900; super. col. surg., S. Stltmts., 1st Mar., 1901; col. surg., Prov. Wellesley, Aug., 1905.

SHEPSTONE, H. C., C.M.G. (1895).—Priv. sec. to the lieut.-gov., Natal, 1857; clk. to exec. coun., 1863; Indian immigr. agt., 1864; R.M. and admstr. of native law, Alfred co., 1870; ditto, Durban co., 1878; acted as sec. to Mr. Justice Phillips, C.M.G., on special service to Barbados, 1876; served on the staff of Sir Theophilus Shepstone, K.C.M.G., H.M.’s special comanr. in S. Africa, 1877; sec. for native affairs, Transvaal, July, 1877; attended Cetywayo on his visit to England, 1882; sec. for native affairs, Natal, 1884; ret., 1893.

SHEPSTONE, JOHN WESLEY, C.M.G. (1888).—B. 1827; July, 1846, govt. interp., Natal; July, 1847, accompanied Capt. Kyle on special mission to Zulu king; Dec., 1850, accompanied Capt. Gordon on special mission to Pondos; Oct., 1851, interp. to recorder and mag.’s offices; Dec., 1851, asst. R.M., Pietermaritzburg co.; Aug., 1852, R.M., Lower Umvoti, and govt. agt., Noniti country, and J.P.; 1857, commanded native forces against Chief Usidol and tribe, and against Chief Matyana and tribe; Nov., 1858, supt. of the cultivation of cotton; Apr., 1861, ag. sec. for native affairs and judicial assessor; July, 1861, commanded a native force in the Fort Buckingham expdn.; May, 1862, ag. R.M., Inanda div.; Aug., 1863, asst. R.M., Pietermaritzburg co.; ag. R.M., Umvoti co., Sept., 1867; May, 1874, comanr., Klip River and Weenen counties; July, 1874, ag. sec. for native affairs and judicial assessor; Oct., 1874, J.P. for the col.; Sept., 1876, sec. for native affairs and mem. exec. and legis. couns.; Mar., 1878, mem. of the bdry. comanr.; Dec., 1878, delivered ultimatum to Zulu delegs. at Lower Drift, Tugela; Aug., 1879, accompanied Sir Garnot Wolseley to arrange the settlement of Zululand; mentioned in despatches; Dec., 1882, Br. consmr., Zululand; Jan., 1884, judge, native high ct.; ret., 1896.

SHEPSTONE, THEOPHILUS, C.M.G. (1880).—B. 1843; was in command of a Basuto regt. in the Zulu war; mem. of Natal legis. coun. until 1887; counsellor with Umbandeen, King of Swaziland, 1887-91.

SHERIFF, PERCY MUSGRAVE CRESSWELL.—Called to the bar, Mid. Temple, June, 1892; admitted to the bar of B. Hond., 1893; of Jamaica, 1895; ag. dist. consmr., Belize, for six months in 1898; apptd. mag. and coroner, So. dist., Grenada, 1900; visiting just. of prisons, 1900; chairman of St. George’s Road Board, 1901; ag. mem. legis. coun., June, 1902; ag. ch. just. and prov. mem. of ex. coun., St. Vincent, Dec., 1902; admtd. govt. and acted as col. sec. and treas., Aug., 1903; ch. just., St. Vincent, Oct., 1903; appt., confirmed, Dec., 1903; M.L.C., Apl., 1904.

SHEELS, THE HON. WILLIAM.—Atty.-gen., Victoria, 1891; premier and treasr., 1892-3.

SHIPWAY, WALTER ROBERT.—Apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd div. clk., and assigned to C.O., Dec., 1898.
SHOLL, L. H., I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1844; clk., P.W. office, S. Australia, July, 1858; clk., waterwks. dept., Jan., 1859; clk., audit office, Sept., 1868; ch. clk., Jan., 1872; ch. clk. and acctnt., treasy., July, 1874; acctnt. and receiver of rev., treasy., July, 1876; cashier and acctnt., treasy., July, 1879; under-treasr., July, 1883; under-sec. and govt. statist., May, 1890; also clk. of exec. coun., July, 1894.

SHORT, EDWARD MORRISON DE COURCY.—Ceylon writer, 1878; pol. mag., 1883; astt. to govt. agt., S. prov., 1886; astt. collr. of cust., and landing survr., cust., Galle, May, 1886; ag. astt. govt. agt., Mannar, Jan., 1889; Hambantota Sect., 1889; Kegalla, May, 1890; Vavuniya and Mullaitivu, Dec., 1890; Kalutara, Apr., 1894; Chilaw, Dec., 1895; Vavuniya, Apr., 1896; Matara, Nov., 1897; astt. govt. agt., Matale, Jan., 1900; Nuwara Eliya, 15 Aug., 1900; ag. pol. mag., Galle, Oct., 1890; dist. judge, Matara, Feb., 1892; astt. govt. agt., Matale, 16th Jan., 1900; ditto, Nuwara Eliya, 15th Aug., 1900.

SHOWERS, EDWARD MELIAN.—Served in Bengal police, Feb., 1867, to Sept., 1901; comsnr. of pol., Transvaal, 8th Nov., 1901.

SIDNEY, T. S., M.A.—Ed. Harvard, and Trin. Hall, Camb.; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., June, 1885; enrolled adv. to high ct. of Madras, 1894; apptd. dist. comsnr., Epe, Lagos, Jan., 1901.

SIERRA LEONE, BISHOP OF, Rt. REV. EDMUND HENRY ELWIN, M.A., Merton Coll., Oxon; cur. of St. Peter-le-Bailey, Oxford, 1894-6; chaplain at Fourah Bay Coll., S. Leone, 1896-8; principal, 1898-1901; chapln. to Bp. of S. Leone, 1898-1901; Bishop of Sierra Leone, 1901.

SIMPSON, GEORGE.—Inspr. of schls., Bermuda, 1889; also inspr. of dockyard schls.

SINCKLER, E. G.—Entered col. sec.'s office, Barbados, Nov. 1874; acted as clk. to lieut.-gov., 1878; 2nd clk. corprnde. branch, col. sec.'s office, 1879; ag. astt. clk. to Gov. W. Robinson, 1880; 1st clk., record branch, col. sec.'s office, and clk., courts of ordinary and error, Jan., 1883; ag. ch. clk., 1886; comsnr. of census, 1891; ch. clk. to judges, 1892; J.P., Oct., 1892; ag. registr., friendly socs., June, 1893; ag. sen. pol. mag., Bridgetown, and dist. A, Aug. to Oct., 1893; ag. pol. mag. and judge, dist. B, Sept. to Oct., 1894; has acted several times as coroner, dist. A; ag. pol. mag. and judge, dist. F, July, 1896, to Jan., 1897; ag. pol. mag., judge, and coroner, dist. B, Sept. to Oct., 1897; ag. pol. mag. and judge, dist. D, Mar. to Apr., 1898; ag. coroner, St. Michael, 1898 (at time of hurricane), and has repeatedly acted as such; ag. pol. mag. and judge, dist. B, 1899; ag. pol. mag., dist. A, Feb., 1900; ag. comsnr. of probate, May to Nov., 1900; ag. pol. mag., dist. A, July, 1900, to Sept., 1901; pol. mag. and judge, dist. E, Oct., 1901.

SINCLAIR, WM.—Ck., stores dept., L. and N.W. rly., Jan., 1863; stores auditor, July, 1875; rly. storekeeper, Midland system, Cape govt. rly., Aug., 1878; ch. rly. storekeeper, Jan., 1886; storekeeper, C.S.A.K., 1904.

SINGAPORE, LABUAN, AND SARAWAK, 3rd BISHOP OF LABUAN, THE RIGHT REV. GEORGE FREDERICK HOSE, D.D.—Ed. St. John's Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1861; M.A., 1867; D.D., 1881; curate of Roxton with Great Barford, Beds., 1861-65; curate of Trinity, St. Marylebone, London, 1865-67; col. chaplain, Malacca, Nov., 1867; ditto, Singapore, Feb., 1874; registr. of the diocese of Labuan, Apr., 1874; archdeacon of Singapore, Dec., 1874; bishop of Singapore, Labuan and Sarawak, 1881.

SIVEWRIGHT, THE HON. SIR JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1892), C.M.G. (1880).—B. 1848; gen. man. of telegraphy, C. of Good Hope, Apr., 1878; ret., 1885; M.L.A., 1889; mem. of Rhodes's ministry without portfolio, July, 1900, and subsequently as comsnr. of crown lands and pub. wks.; resig., 1893; resumed office, Jan., 1896.

SKEEN, G. J. A.—Extra astt. govt. printer, Ceylon, 1869; astt. govt. printer, 1872; govt. printer, 1881.

SKEETE, ELLIOT L., B.A., Durham, 1888.—Ast. to supt. bot. station, Barbados, Sept., 1890; ag. supt., Dec., 1890, to Jan., 1891; ch. offr. reformatory, May, 1892; ag. supt. reformatory and bot. station, July to Dec., 1894, and Apr. to May, 1895; and other occasions.

SKERETT, CHRISTOPHER MARTIN.—Supernumerary clk., regiar. and provost marshal's office, Dominica, July to Dec., 1891, and Feb. to Sept., 1892; astt. clk. to govt. offr., Roseau, Sept., 1892, to Mar., 1893; aid waiter, treasy., Aug. to Oct., 1893; tax collr., treasy., Nov., 1893, to Apr., 1894; astt. clk., tax dept., treasy., 1895; astt. to admstr., Jan. to Mar., 1896; 2nd clk., regiar. and prov. marshal's off., Dominica, Mar., 1898, to Dec., 1899; 1st clk., Jan., 1901; is a comsnr. to admstr. oaths, Dominica; and supt. of pub. cemetery; has held numerous "acting" appointments.

SKINNER, WM., M.A.—Ed. Belford gram. schl.; scholar St. Catherine's Coll., Camb. B.A. (math. tripos), 1882; M.A., Oct., 1886; headmnr., Govt. gram. schl., Dominica, Dec., 1892.

SLATER, A. R.—Ed. at King Ed. schl., Birmingham, and Emm. coll., Camb. (A.B.), 1887; cadet, Ceylon, Nov., 1898; extra off., astt. govt. agent, W. P., Aug., 1899; 2nd astt., P.M.G., Mar., 1900; ag. 2nd astt. col. sec., Dec., 1901; on spec. duty at camp for prisoners of war Diyalatalawa, July, 1902; ag. 2nd astt. col. sec., Jan., 1903; clk. leg. coun., May, 1904.

SLATTERY, THE HON. T. M.—Mem. legis. assem., N.S. Wales; sec. for mines and agricul. in Dibbs's ministry, 1891-94.

SLOLEY, HERBERT CECIL, C.M.G. (1905).—Served in C.M.R. in campaigns against Griquas and Moirosi (medal with clasp, 1877-8-9); capt. in native contingent, Basuto war, 1880-1; mentioned in despatches; sub-inspr., Cape police, 1883; ditto, Basutoland, 1884; inspr., 1886; astt. comsnr., Basutoland, 1889; ag. res. comsnr., July to Dec., 1895; govt. sec., 1898; ag. res. comsnr., Dec., 1900; res. comsnr., Sept., 1901.

SLYNE, D.—Barrister-at-law; Lord O'Hagan medallist and David Lynch medallist, King's Inns, Ireland; entered Imperial civ. serv., open compet., 1880; until 1900 attached successively to Inland Rev. Dept. at Dublin, Sligo, Chester, Oxford, Leicester, Birmingham, Dublin, Dundee, and Birmingham; apptd. supervising excise offr., Trinidad, 1900; ag. receiver-gen., May, 1902; receiver-gen., Feb., 1903.

SMALLWOOD, HENRY ARMSTRONG.—Entered navy, 1885; on board H.M.S. "Victoria" at time of disaster, June, 1893; astt. comsnr., Colo West and stip. mag., Apr., 1894; ag. stip. mag., Ba and Yasawa, Apr., 1896; 2nd clk., col. sec.'s office, and priv. sec. to gov. Fiji, Apr., 1896; ag. sec. to W. Pac. high comsn., May, 1897, to May, 1898; stip. mag., Savu Savu and Taviuni, Jan., 1899; island treasr., Cyprus, Mar., 1900.

SMART, ARCHIBALD WM.—Ck., dept. of trade and cust., Melbourne, 1863; landing waiter, 1868; landing survr., 1890; senior ditto, 1893; collr. & cust., Victoria, and regiar. of shipping, Melbourne, 1903; ch. Commonwealth survr., 1903.
SMARTT, JAMES A.—Alderman of Brandon, Manitoba, 1882-84; mayor, 1885-87; mem. judicial bd., 1886; mem. of prov. legislature, 1886; min. of pub. wks., 1888; dep. min. of the interior of Canada, Apr., 1897; dept. supt.-gen. of Indian affairs, July, 1897.

SMARTT, CAPT. J. P. (3rd Batt., South Lancs. Regt.),—Public wks. and roads dept., G. Coast, 1893-96; local auditor, N. C. Prot. (now S. Nigeria), Oct., 1896; chief asst. treas., Dec., 1901; ag. treas., Dec., 1901, to June, 1902, and June to Dec., 1903; lieut. G. C. rifle volrs., May, 1893; capt., Nov., 1893; ag. adjt., May to Nov., 1893; ag. comdt., Oct., 1895, to Mar., 1896; attached for duty with Niger C. Protec. force, May to July, 1897, May and Aug., 1900; ag. treas., So. Nigeria, June to Dec., 1903, and in Sept., 1904; served with expdt. Benin territories, Apr. and May, 1899; mentl. in depts. medal and clasp; bronze medal R. Hum. Soc., 1887.

SMARTT, DR. THOS. WM.—L.R.C.S., Ireland, 1878; L.K.Q.C.P.I., 1880; M.L.A. for Wodehouse, Cape Colony, 1894; col. sec., 1898; comsnr. of pub. wks., 1900-02, and from Feb., 1904; ag. prime minister during periods of 1904 and 1906; holds Cape Colony general service medal, 1879, with clasp, "Transkei," having served as surg. with P.A.O.C.V.A.; also holds medal and clasp for Kimberley siege, 1899-1900.

SMERDON, S. P., I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1842; extra clk. in office of S. of S. forCols., June, 1862; 1st class clk. in col. sec.'s office, Jamaica, June, 1870; regar. gen. of births, deaths and marriages, 8th Feb., 1878; suptd. the taking of census of Jamaica, 1881 and 1891; dep. keeper of records (on amalgamation of registration and record depts.), May, 1899; nom. mem. of comsn. to inquire into marriage and reglan. laws, May, 1903.

SMITH, ALLAN F.—Clk. in P.O., Bermuda, 1879; clk., col. sec.'s office, 1886; asst. col. sec., 1895; col. postmnr., 1896; ag. col. sec., July and Aug., 1899, and from May, 1900, to July, 1901.

SMITH, SIR C. ABERCHROMBIE, KT. BACH. (1903).—M.A. (Camb. and Glas.), fellow of St. Peter's Coll., Camb., 2nd wrangler and 2nd Smith's prize man, 1885, &c.; mem. of the house of assem., Cape, 1866-75; mem. of the exec. coun., 1872; comsnr. of crown lands and pub. works, 1872-75; mem. of comte, under Ordinance 97, 1872-5; comsnr. of the sinking fund, 1872-4; mem. of the Univ. coun., 1873; chmn. of the meteorol. comsn., 1874; comptroller and audr.-gen., 1875; chmn. of the tender bd., 1876; mem. of the surety bd., 1875-86; vice-chancellor, Cape Univ., 1877-9; comsnr., civ. ser. exams. bd., 1886; chairman, 1887; ret., 1904.

SMITH, C. A. JEFFREY.—Apprentice, pub. wks. dept., Jamaica, Aug., 1870; asst. to ch. supt., 1875; 3rd class ditto, 1879; 2nd class ditto, 1881; ag. dist. engnr., W. dist., 1886; ditto, Kingston dist., 1888-9; overseer of wks., prisons dept., 1889; 1st cls. supt., pub. wks., and supt., St. Catherine waterwks., 1896; also acted on several occasions as govt. assessor, and supt. irrigation wks.

SMITH, SIR CECIL CLEMENTI, G.C.M.G. (1892), K.C.M.G. (1886), C.M.G. (1880).—B. 1840; ed. at St. Paul's Schl. and Corp. Chr. Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1862, M.A., 1868; elected student interp., Hong Kong, Mar., 1862; regar.-gen., Mar., 1865; ag. pol. mag., June, 1865; ag. col. sec., 1867; mem. of exec. coun., 1869; ag. col. sec., Feb., 1872, to Dec., 1873; treas., 1871; acted as col. sec., Oct., 1874, and also from Mar., 1876; col. sec., S. Sttlmte., July, 1878; apptd. under the F.O. to be Br. comsnr. to settle certain marine claims at Manila, Sept., 1878, and received the thanks of H.M.'s govt.; also for services in connection with the "Niseru" case, 1884; administered govt. S.S., Mar., 1884, to Nov., 1885; lieut.-gov. and col. sec., Ceylon, Nov., 1885; gov. of S. S., 1887; also consul-gen. and high commr. for Borneo and Sarawak, 1889; ret., 1893; pres. of comsn. to inquire into Trinidad riots, 1903.

SMITH, SIR CHARLES HOLLED, K.C.M.G., C.B.—B. 1846; ensign, 1863; lieut., 1869; capt., 1877; S. African war, 1879-1881; Zulu campaign; Transvaal cam., battles of Laing's Nek, Ingogo, and Majuba Mountain; despatches, Lon. Gaz. May 3, 1881; Egyp. expedn., 1882; at Ramleh, Tel-el-Mahuta; action at Kassassin; battle of Tel-el-Kebir, Lon. Gaz., Nov. 2, 1882; major (brevet), Nov., 1882; with Egyp. army, Jan., 1883, to Aug., 1892; Soudan expedn., 1884-5; lieut.-col., June, 1885; col., Dec., 1888; gov.-gen., Red Sea littoral, and comdt. Suakin, Sept., 1888, to Aug., 1892; Soudan, 1888-91; action of Gamaizah, Lon. Gaz., Jan. 11, 1889; occupation of Handoul, Jan., 1891; major-gen. comdg. Victorian mil. forces, Dec., 1894; several medals, clasps to bronze stars, and mentioned in numerous despatches.

SMITH, EDWIN MITCHELL.—Entered survey, crown lands dept., S. Australia, as astt., June, 1862; cadet and jun. survr.; survr., Jan. 1869; draftman, Jan., 1874; steward and survr. of educnl. lands, Feb., 1882; ch. clk. and land office, Jan., 1886; dep. survr.-gen., July, 1894; mem. of central pastoral and central lands bds.

SMITH, FRANCIS.—Ch. mag., Gambia, 1879; puisne judge, G. Coast Col., 1887.

SMITH, FRANCIS JAGOE.—M.A. Oxon.; ed. Merchant Taylors schl.; scholar, St. John's Coll., Oxford, 1892; 2nd cls. class. mods., 1894; 2nd math. mods., 1894; 2nd Lit. Hum., 1896; B.A., 1896; M.A., 1902; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Oct., 1896; attached to col. sec.'s off., 1896; office astt. to govt. agt., and deputy fiscal, Cent. Prov., Apr., 1898; comsnr. of requests and pol. mag., Balapitiya, Aug., 1900; ditto, Galle, June, 1901; landing survr., customs, Colombo, Dec., 1901.

SMITH, THE HON. SIR FRANCIS, KNT. (creat. 1862).—B. 1819; B.A. Lond. Univ., 1840; called to the bar, Mid. Temp., May, 1842; solr.-gen., Tasmania, 1840; atty.-gen., 1854; mem. of the legis. assem., 1849-60, and of the exec. coun., 1855-60; atty. gen. upon the introduction of responsible govt. in 1866; prime min., 1857; raised to the bench as a puisne judge of the sup. ct., 1860; ch. just., May, 1870; was admstr. of the govt., 1874; again, 1880; ret., 1885.

SMITH, FRANK BRAYBROOKE.—Director of agric., Transvaal, and agric. adviser to the govt., Apr., 1902; M.L.C.

SMITH, FREDERICK BONHAM, I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1837; entered col. sec.'s office, Barbados, 1859; in office of gov.-in-chief of the Windward Is., 1860 to 1866; pol. mag. of Christchurch, Barbados, 1866; sen. pol. mag. of Bridgetown and St. Michael, 1873; ag. judge of the asst. ct. of appeal, 1878 to 1890; inspr. of prisons, 1878, held with office of provost-marshal from 1882; ag. col. sec., 1879.

SMITH, FREDERICK STANLEY.—Ed. at Sherborne Coll., Eng.; called to the bar, In. Temp., Jan., 1892; ag. pol. mag., dist. "B," Barbados, Aug. to Oct., 1893; ag. pol. mag. dist. "D," Apr., 1894, to July, 1895; and from Dec., 1895, to Oct., 1896; ag. pol. mag. dist. "C," Jan. to Feb., 1897; J.P., Apr., 1897; ag. judge-asst., ct. of appeal, Apr. to Sept., 1897; ag. pol. mag., dist. "E," Jan., 1898; ag. pol. mag., Bridgetown
and dist. "A." Feb. to May, 1898; ag. pol. mag., dist. "F," Sept. to Oct., 1898; apptd. pol. mag., dist. "D," Jan., 1899; ag. pol. mag., Bridgetown and dist. "A." Nov., 1901, to Apr., 1902.

SMITH, GEORGE.—Transf. from W.O. to ch sec.'s office, Cyprus, Nov., 1879; ch. clk., 1881; asst. to ch. sec., 1883 to 1891; clk., legis. coun., 1886 to 1891; sec. to the comttee. for the representation of Cyprus at the Col. and Ind. Exhibition; ag. ch. sec., May to Oct., 1888; comsnr. of Papho, 1891; regis.-gen. and mem. legis. coun., 1895.

SMITH, GEORGE.—Ed. at Galway House Schl., Leyton, Essex, and at Morden House, Greenwich; ag. dist. comsnr., Anamabeo, G. Coast, 1877; dist. comsnr., Dexevoe, 1878; ditto, Palma and Leckie, Lagos, 1880; sub-collr. customs, Palma and Leckie, 1883; ch. clk. and warehouse keeper, customs, Lagos, Aug., 1889; ag dist. comsnr., E. dist., Lagos, Mar., 1892.

SMITH, GEORGE DOUGLAS, C.M.G. (1905).—Joined Imperial Brit. East Africa Co., 1890; treas., Uganda Prot., Mar., 1894.

SMITH, CAPT. GEORGE ECKLIN.—Ed. Rathmines Schl. and Trin. Coll., Dublin; joined 5th Batt., Royal Irish Regt., 1891; capt., 1895; hon. capt. in army, 1900; asst. inspr., G. Coast constab., 1897; sub-inspr., B. Guiana police, 1897; dist. inspr., 1900; A.D.C. to Sir F. Hodgson, K.C.V.O., gov. of B. Guiana.

SMITH, GEORGE WHITFIELD.—F.L.S., Clk., pub. library, Barbados, Sept., 1879; 3rd treasy. clk., St. Lucia, 1882; sub-collr. of taxes, 1st dist., St. Lucia, Aug., 1882; rev. offr., Leeward dist., St. Vincent, Feb., 1885 (resigned); curator, botanic gardens, Grenada, Dec., 1890, (resigned, 16th Dec., 1893); trav. supt., Imperial dept. of agric., Dec., 1898; pol. mag. and asst. treas., N. dist. Grenada, and pol. mag., 3rd dist., St. Vincent, Apr., 1904; comsnr., Carriacou, Oct., 1904; was engaged as asst. botanist to W. India exploration comttee. of Royal Soc. during scientific exploration of St. Vincent, 1888-89; is a corrpdg. mem. of Royal Hort. Soc. of England.

SMITH, GERALD STANLEY WELLS.—Graduate Ontario business coll., Canada; supery. clk., registr.'s office, Grenada, Jan., 1890; asst. clk., post office, Mar., 1890; 4th clk., treasy., June, 1890; asst. clk., col. sec.'s office, Oct., 1890; 2nd clk., treasy., Nov., 1891; audit clk., Nov., 1897; has held numerous acting appointments.

SMITH, Lieut.-Col. Sir GERARD, K.C.M.G. (1896).—B.1839; late lieut.-col. Roy. Scots Guards; groom-in-waiting to Her Majesty, 1883-5; M.P. for High Wycombe, 1883-5; J.P. for E. Riding of Yorkshire; gov. of W. Australia, 1895 to 1900.

SMITH, HENRY J.—Apptd., after exam., 3rd cl. messenger C.O., 12th Nov., 1883; 2nd cl. ditto, 1st June, 1897; Queen's mess., 1st Apr., 1898.

SMYTH, H. WASHINGTON.—Ed. at Westmstr. and Trin. Coll., Camb., M.A., L.L.M., F.G.S., F.R.G.S., barr-at-law; unpaid asst. to mineral adviser to office of woods, 1891; sec., dept. of mines, Siam, 1891; director-gen. of mines and geological survey, Siam, 1895; sec., Siamese Legation, 1897 (order of White Elephant, 3rd cl.); sec. to mines dept., Transvaal, 1901; author of "Five Years in Siam," "Mast and Sail in Europe and Asia," papers on Indo-China, etc., etc.

SMITH, JAMES ALFRED.—Apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv., and assigned to the C.O., Apr., 1891; promoted to higher grade, 1902.

SMITH, JAR. C.—Ch. clk. and storekr., Imperial treasy. and commissariat depts., Bahamas, June, 1876, to Aug., 1889; mem. bd. of educ., 1886 to 1892; postmr., 1889; J.P., 1890; elected mem. of Bahamas House of Assembly in 1882-89 and 1896; resigned 1897; asst. postmr. gen., Sierra Leone, Dec., 1896; J.P., 1897; ag. postmr. gen., 1897, 1899, and 1900; ag. curator of intestates, S. L., from Jan., 1899, to Jan., 1900.

SMITH, JAMES LANDRETH.—Draftsman, P.W.D., St. Lucia, 13th July, 1891; draftsman, survey off., Sept., 1893; warden, and supt. of water-wks. under St. George's town bd., Apr., 1895, to Aug., 1901; chief overseer of roads and works, Grenada, 19th Aug., 1901; asst. supt. of wks., 1st Apr., 1902; comsnr. of crown lands, 28th June, 1904.

SMITH, JAMES PARKER, M.P.; P.C.(1904).—Ed. Winchester, and Trin. Coll., Camb. (4th wrangler and 2nd Smith's prizeman, 1877; fellow of Winchester and late fellow Trin. Coll.); called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1881; J.P. and D.L., Renfrewshire and co. of city of Glasgow; J.P., Lanarkshire; dir. of Union Bank of Scotland; elected for Partick div. of Lanarkshire, 1890; parly. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, 1901-3.

SMITH, Sir JOHN SMALMAN, KT. BACH. (1896).—M.A., St. John's Coll., Camb.; b. 1847; called to the bar, In. Tem., 1872; special pleader Oxford circuit; puisne judge, G. Coast Col., 1883; judge, Lagos, 1886; ch. just., Lagos, 1889; ret., 1895.

SMITH, LINDSAY LEA.—Acting clk. to comnr., Turks Is., 1894, 1896, 1900, and 1903; confirmed 1st July, 1903.

SMITH, RICHARD WILLIAM, A.M.I.C.E., B.A., B.A.I.—P. W. Dept., Ceylon; ed. at the Grammar Schl., Chard, Somerset, 1874, and Dublin Univ. (Trinity College), 1875-79; employed in engineer's off., D.W.W. Rlwy., 1879; res. engr., Wicklow Harb. works, 1880-83; asst. to Mr. J. Lanyon, Belfast (rlwys., waterwks., drainage, etc.), 1883-85; res. engr., Cleggan Harb. Works, 1885-88; asst. res. engr., St. Helier's Harb. Works (Jersey), 1888-89; supt. P.W., Pahang, S.S., 1889-92; D.E., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1892-94; ag. prov. engr., N.W.P., 1894-97; dist. engr. and ag. prov. engr., S.P., 1898; seconded to railway extensions staff, 1898; seconded to "Water Supply Schemes," 1898-1900; charge of Boer Camp Works, 1900; "Water Supply Schemes," 1901-02; seconded as res. engr., proposed convict prison works, Seychelles, 1902; returned to Ceylon 13th Aug., 1902.

SMITH, ROBERT MURRAY, C.M.G. (1884).—B. 1831; agt.-gen. for Victoria in United Kingdom, 1881-86.

SMITH, HON. SYDNEY.—M.P. for Macquarie, New South Wales; postmr.-gen., Commonwealth of Australia, in Reid-Turner ministry, 1904.

SMITH, THOMAS SERCOMBE, B.A., LL.B. (Lond.).—Hong Kong cadet, 1882; attached to C.O., 1883; passed cadet, 1886; ag. asst. regist. gen., 1886-90, except for five months as ag. pol. mag.; asst. regist.-gen., 1891; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., Nov., 1893; ag. puisne judge, various dates, 1895-7, and in 1900, 1901, 1902, 1904 and 1905; treas. Dec., 1896; pol. mag., July, 1898; ag. col. sec., 1898-9, and for 3 months in 1901.

SMITH, WM. EDWARD.—Employed on L. & N.W. Rly., 1872-82; asst. traffic man., Indian guaranteed rlys. (Scinde, Punjab, and Delhi), 1883-86; ag. district traffic man., Lahore and Delhi div.; gen. man., Barbados Rly., 1889; gen. and traffic man., Trinidad and Govt. Rly., Feb., 1894; received special allowance of 100l. in 1895 for reorganising rly. dept.; is a J.P.
SMITH, SIR WILLIAM FREDERICK HAYNES, K.C.M.G. (1890), C.M.G. (1887).—B. 1839; called to the bar, Mid. Term., June, 1863; solr.-gen., Br. Guiana, Oct., 1865; atty.-gen., Oct., 1874; admstr. the govt., Apr. to Sept., 1884, and in 1887; gov., Leeward Is., Nov., 1888; gov., Bahamas, 1895; high commr., Cyprus, 1892-1904.

SMITH, SIR WILLIAM JAMES, KT. BACH. (1896).—M.A., LL.M. Trinity Hall, Camb.; b. 1863; acted as puisne judge of the G. Coast Coll. from Dec. 1880, to July, 1881; puisne judge of the sup. ct. of Cyprus, 1882; ch. just., 1892; ch. just., Br. Guiana, 1898; puisne judge, sup. ct., Transvaal, 1st Mar., 1902.

SMITH, WILLIAM RAMSAY.—B.Sc., M.B., M.S., Edin.; chmn. cent. bd. of health, coroner, vaccination offr., and inspr. of anatomy, S. Australia, 1899-1903; chmn. cent. bd. of health, and coroner, 1903.

SMITH-STEINMETZ, GERARD ARCHIBALD.—Ed. at Stonyhurst coll.; cadet, Straits Settlements, Oct., 1902; in charge of S.S. emigr. depot, S. India, June, 1904; passed final exam. in Tamil, July, 1904; ag. 3rd mag., Penang, Feb., 1905.

SMUTS, JOHANNES.—Ck., treas., Cape, 1882; acted as priv. sec. to the Hon. J. Gordon Sprigg, 1885-6; to Sir H. A. Smyth, 1889; to Lieut.-Gen. H. E. Cameron, and to Sir H. Loch, 1891; sec. to Hon. J. H. Hofmeyr (Swaziland Convention), 1890; asst. dispatch clk., govt. house, 1896; 2nd class clk., 1897; ag. priv. sec. to Lieut.-Gen. Cameron and to Sir H. B. Loch, 1891 to 1895; ch. clk. to high commr., 1891; acted as clk. of exec. coun., 1891 and 1895; Br. consul in Swaziland, Aug., 1895-9.

SMYLY, PHILIP CRAMPTON.—Ed. at Trin. Coll., Dub., B.A., LL.B.; called to the bar, King's Inns, Dub., 1888; LL.D., 1891; Queen's advoc., S. Leone, 1895; atty.-gen., 1896.

SMYTH, C. E. OWEN, I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1851; ed. at Erasmus Smith Schl., Dub.; specification clk., S. Australia, 1876; profnl. clk., 3rd class, 1878; 1st class, 1883; supt. of pub. bldgs., 1886.

SMYTH, GEN. SIR HENRY AUGUSTUS, K.C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1825; in command of the troops, S. Africa, 1889; gov. of Malta, 1890-3.

SNOWBALL, JABEZ BUNTING.—Lieut.-gov., New Brunswick, Canada, 5th Feb., 1902.

SOLOMON, JOHN.—2nd class astt. of excise, England, Apr., 1868; 1st class astt., June, 1870; ride offr., June, 1871; resig., Jan., 1876; ag. 3rd clk., immigr. dept., Br. Guiana, July, 1877; ag. cashier in rec.-gen.'s office, 1878; comsry. of taxation, 1879.

SOLOMON, MICHAEL CLAUDE.—Ag. 3rd cl. clk., island med. dept., Jamaica, Mar., 1885; 3rd cl. clk., Oct., 1888; 2nd cl. clk., July, 1891.

SOLOMON, HON. SIR RICHARD, K.C.B. (1905), K.C.M.G. (1901), C.B. (1903), K.C.—Ed. S. African Coll., Capetown; St. Peter's Coll., Camb., 23rd wrangler; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1879; legal adviser to late Lord Rosemead on his mission to Mauritius, 1886; mem. of native law comsn.; chmn. of mining coman.; mem. of House of Ass. for division of Tembuland, Cape; atty.-gen., Cape, 1898-1900; legal adviser to Transvaal adminstr., 1901-1902; atty.-gen., Transvaal, 19th June, 1902; mem. ex. and leg. couns.; mem. I.C.C.

SOLOMON, WM. HENRY.—B.A., Cantab; admitted to the bar, Inner Temple, 1877; practised in Cape Colony; astt. legal adviser, Cape, 1883; puisne judge, sup. ct., 1887; pres., spec. treason court, 1900; 1st puisne judge, Transvaal, 1902.

SOUZA, SIMON I. DE.—Ed. at the R. Catholic gram schl., Lagos; 1st despatch clk. and shorthand writer, col. sec.'s office, Lagos, June, 1895; acted as clk. of the legis. coun., 1900; regar. of correspondence, June, 1900; conf. clk. to gov. and clk. of leg. coun., July, 1901; ag. priv. sec. to gov., and clk. to ex. coun., Feb., 1902; in charge of Ibadan residency, Nov., 1903.

SORZANO, TILDEBER.—Draughtsman, crown lands office, Trinidad, 1874; first ditto, survey dept., Aug., 1881.

SPALDING, LIEUT.-COL. WARNER WRIGHT, C.M.G. (1886).—B. 1844; N. S. Wales Artill., 1876; in command of the detachment which served in the Sudan, 1884; res. mag. Norfolk Is., 1896.

SPEED, EDWIN ARNEY.—M.A., LL.B.; ed. at Rugby, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; major scholar and senior exhibtnr., Rugby schl.; scholar and prize-man of Trin. Coll., Camb.; 1st cls. class. tripes, 1890; 2nd cls. law tripes, Part I., 1891; called to the bar, Inner Temple, June, 1893; dist. commr., G. Coast, 1898; atty.-gen., Lagos, 1900; edited a revised edition of Lagos laws, 1901; has acted on numerous occasions as ch. just. and also as col. sec., and has held a commr. as dep. govr.

SPENCE, FRANK.—3rd clk. col. sec.'s office, Fiji, 1880; clk. to commrs. of wks., Oct., 1884; ag. priv. sec. to gov., 1884, 1885, and 1887 to 1896; sec. to consul-gen. for W. Pacific, 1889 to 1896; stip. mag., Cakandrove and Bua, 1896 to 1898; provincial inspr. and stip. mag., Cakandrove and Bua, 1899; ditto, Cakandrove, 1901; stip. mag., Navua, Jan., 1904.

SPENCE, J. B.—Med. supt. of Colombo lun. asyl., Ceylon, 1886.

SPENCE, R. O. H.—Cler. asst., P.W. dept., Br. Guiana, 16th Aug., 1886; ag. 2nd clk., P.W. dept., Aug., 1889; ag. 3rd cl. clk., treasy., Jan., 1890; gov. offr., govt. ld. dept., Apr., 1890; clk., govt. ld. dept., May, 1890; sec. Bartika commrs., June, 1891, to May, 1893; clk., dept. mines, Oct., 1892; ag. 3rd cl. clk., dept. mines, Apr., 1893; gov't. offr., dept. mines, July, 1893; J.P., May, 1894; commr. to admr. oaths, June, 1894; dist. govt. offr., dept. mines, Aug., 1896; warden, dept. mines, Nov., 1896; obtld. certif. as sworn land surv., June, 1898; ag. ch. clk., dept. mines, Feb., 1900.

SPENCER, CYRIL E.—Ck., ch. sec.'s office, Cyprus, 1st Aug., 1892; passed in Mod. Greek, lower standard, Nov., 1893; clk., legis. coun., Mar., 1894; ag. priv. sec. to O.A.G., Jan.-Apr., 1898; inspr. of pol., May, 1898; ag. priv. sec. and clk. to ex. coun., Feb.-May, 1899, and Dec., 1899, to May, 1900; ag. local comdt. of police, Papho, July, 1900, to June, 1901; Limassol, from June, 1901.

SPICER, QUINTEN HERBERT.—2nd clk., col. sec.'s dept., Tobago, 1884; 1st clk., audit and registry dept., 1884; 2nd rev.offr., 1885; harbrmr. and landing waiter, 1889; supervisor of excise, 1892; inspr. of pol., 1896; in charge of prison, 1897; asst. harbrmr., Trinidad, 1899.

SPIRE, JOHN.—Apptd., after exam., 3rd class messenger, C.O., Jan., 1883; 2nd class, July, 1896; Queen's mess., Nov., 1899.

SPRIGG, THE RT. HON. SIR JOHN GORDON, P.C. (1897), G.C.M.G. (1902), K.C.M.G. (1886).—B. 1830; represented E. London in Casa assm. 1869-1904; col. sec. and premier, Feb., 1878, to May, 1881; col. treas., May, 1884, to Nov., 1886; premier, Nov., 1886; apptd. comdr. legion of honour for services in Paris Exhibn., 1889; resig. office, July, 1890; again treas., 1893, and also
premier 1896; represented the col. in London at H.M.'s Diam. Jub. resig. premiership, Oct., 1898; again premier 1900-04.

SPROULE, PERCY JULIAN, B.A., Camb.—Bar-rister-at-law (Mid. Tem.) ; cadet, S.S., Nov., 1893; ag. dep. regist., sup. ct., Penang, Mar., 1897; passed final in Malay, Mar., 1899; ag 3rd mag., Penang, June, 1899; dep. regist., sup. ct., Penang, Sept., 1899; ag. asst. regist., sup. ct., Penang, May, 1903; ag. 2nd mag., Sing., Sept., 1904; ag. dep. pub. pros., May, 1905.

STAGG, SIDNEY.—Apptd., after compct. exam., elk. 2nd div. civil ser., and assigned to board of agriculture, Dec., 1897; transfed. to C.O., Mar., 1899; regist. of col. laws, Jan., 1906.

STANFORD, WALTER ERNEST MORTIMER, C.B. (1900). C.M.G. (1892).—B. 1850; mag.'s clk., Cape Col., 1863; mag., 1876; capt. of levies in Gcaleka war, 1877-8 (medal); mem. native laws and customs comm., 1880-2; comdt. in war of 1880-1; on special service to Pondoland, 1884; ch. mag. Griqualand E., 1885; negotiated treaty with Pondos, 1886; sec. nat. affairs dept., 1898; ditto and ch. mag., July, 1904; mem. of S. African native affairs comm., Sept., 1903, to Jan., 1905; holds rank of colonel in Cape colonial forces.

STANMORE, THE RIGHT HON. SIR ARTHUR HAMILTON GORDON, 1st Baron (creat. 1893), G.C.M.G. (1878), K.C.M.G. (1871), C.M.G. (1859).—B. 1829; priv. sec. to his father, Earl of Aberdeen, when 1st lord of the treas., 1832 to 1855; M.P. for Beverley from July, 1854, till Mar., 1857; accompanied Mr. Gladstone on his special mission as lord high comntr. extraord. to the Ionian Is., Nov., 1858; capt. comdt. of the 1st Aberdeenshire R.V., Feb., 1860; licut.-gov. of N. Brunswick, Oct., 1861; gov. of Trinidad, Nov., 1866; gov. of Mauritius, 1870; ret., 1874; gov. of the new col. of Fiji, Jan., 1875; H.M.'s high comntr. and consul-gen. for the W. Pacific, 1877; gov. of N. Zealand, 1880; gov. of Ceylon, 1883; ret., 1890.

STANTON, LIONEL WM.—Inspr. of schls., S. Aust., 1876; asst. insprn.-gen., 1892; chmn. of bd. of insprns., 1896; insprn.-gen. of schls., 1902.

STERLE, WALTER MATTHEW.—Clerical asst., treasy., Br. Guiana, Feb., 1884; 5th class clk., Feb., 1886; 4th class, July, 1888; 3rd class, Apr., 1890; ag. clk.-in-charge, sub-treasy. and savings bk., Dec., 1891, to June, 1893; 2nd class clk. (acctnt.), govt. land dept., April, 1896; asst. treas., So. Nigeria, July, 1904.

STEEN, DAVID MILLER, B.A.—Scholar, Queen's Coll., Belfast; 1st class exhibitioner, Roy. Univ.; B.A. 1895; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 1887; pol. mag., Balapitiya, 1889; asst. collr., customs, Trincomalee, 1890; ditto, Galle, 1892; pol. mag., Haldemulla, 1893; ag. dist. judge, Badulla, 1893; ag. dist. judge, Tangalla, 1895.

STEERE, C. J. LEE.—Probation clk., col. sec.'s off., W. Aust., Feb., 1885; jun. clk., Aug., 1885; ag. clk., gov.'s off., 1889-1890; clk. of leg. coun. and clk. of parlts., Dec., 1890, to June, 1901; elk. of leg. asscnn., June, 1901.

STEIN, JOHN.—Ed. at Christ's Coll., Finchley, and at Neuwied, Germany; sec. to consulates for Germany, Sweden and Norway, and Denmark, in Mauritius, May, 1889, to Dec., 1896; apptd. by S. of S., F.O., as asst. dist. comntr. in H.B.M.'s Niger Coast Protectorate, April, 1897; ag. dist. comntr., Opopo, June, 1897, to June, 1898; Bonny, Jan., 1899, to Jan., 1900; promoted dist. comntr., Jan., 1900; asst. sec. to govt., Southern Nigeria, June, 1900; ag. sec. to govt., Sept., 1900, to May, 1901, and from June to Nov., 1901; West African medal with clasp, 1899; ment. in desps. for services in connection with Aro expedition, 1901-2; ret., 1904.

STEPHEN, CHELVUM.—Ind. interp. to res. mag., Durban, Natal, Jan., 1875; clk. and Ind. interp. to res. mag., Umlazi div., co. of Durban, Mar., 1875; Tamil interp., sup. ct., 1885.

STEPHEN, GUY NEVILLE.—Ed. Paris, Marseilles, London; M.R.C.S., Eng., 1881; licentiate of medicine, France, 1882; ag. house surg., Lincoln co. hosp.; ditto, asst. med. offr., Middlesex co. asylum (Colney Hatch); surg. to the consulate of Norway and Sweden, Marseilles, 1881; surg. to the Br. Consulate and Seamen's Home, Marseilles, 1882; dist. med. offr., Nicosia, Cyprus, 1883; med. offr., central prison, gen. and ophthalmic hosp.; med. offr. of health, Nicosia, 1889; ag. ch. med. offr., 1885 and 1890; surg. to Smyrna Hosp., 1894.

STEPHEN, SIR MATTHEW HENRY, KT. BACH. (1904).—Mem. legis. assem., N.S.W., 1869-71; judge, sup. ct., May, 1887.

STEPHEN, WILLIAM WILBERFORCE.—Clk., col. secretariat, N. S. Wales, 1862; priv. sec. to various premiers, 1856-58; clk., land dept., 1858; under-sec. for lands, 1870; sec., atty.-gen.'s dept., 1880.

STEPHENS, THOMAS NOAKES.—Jun. offr., S. Australia; customs, 1864; clk., marine bd., 1865; boarding offr., customs, 1866; asst. landing waiter, 1867; confil. clk., 1870; ch. clk., treasy., 1875; sec. marine bd., 1877; sec. of customs, 1889; under-treas., 1890; collr. of customs, regis. of shipping, ch. inspr. of distilleries and excise, pres. of marine bd., 1894; is a J.P.; transfed. with cust. dept. to serv. of Commonwealth of Aust., 1st Jan., 1901.

STEPHENSON ALBERT EDWARD.—Clk. E. and A. dept., Feb., 1884; local auditor, Lagos, Aug., 1888, also ag. local auditor, G. Coast, Dec., 1888, to Aug., 1889; returned to E. and A. depts., and apptd. to col. audit branch, Jan., 1891; clk. in charge of acct., May, 1893; asst. supt., Aug., 1897.

STEVENS, FRED. G.—B.A. Oxon.; ed. at Winchester and New Coll., Oxford; cadet, Straits Settlements, Oct., 1902; demarcation offr., Sing., 15th June, 1903; dep. coll. of land rev. and regis. of deeds, Sing., in addtn. to other duties, Oct., 1903; ag. dist. offr., Malacca, June, 1904; passed final exam. in Malay, July, 1904; ag. head, Malay Coll., Dec., 1906.

STEVENS, PERCIVAL.—Asst. M.I.C.E.; asst. engrn. govt. rlys., Trinidad, 1874; dist. engrn., Couva extension rly., 1878; res. engrn. in charge of construction, San Fernando and Guasaca rlys., 1879; 1st asst. engrn., P.W. dept., Jan., 1885; has acted as asst. dir. of P.W., 1885, 6, 8, 9, and 9a; engrn., N. div., P.W.D., Jan., 1892; 1st engrn. in charge of rds. and bdges., P.W.D., Jan., 1894; engrn. in charge of rds. and bdges, rds. and bdges. dept., Jan., 1895; ag. dir. pub. wks., with seat in legis. coun., May, 1894, to Feb., 1895.

STEWARD, MAJ.-GEN. EDWARD HARDING, C.M.G. (1887).—B. 1836; entered army, Roy. Engrns., Oct., 1854; employed from 1865 to 1879 in the fortification branch of the W.O.; services lent in 1866 to 1869, and in 1877 to the S. Australian govt., and in 1877 till 1879 to the govt. of Victoria. In charge of the defence of the Natal frontier in 1879, and comdt. of Natal and mem. of exec. coun. of the col. in 1880; services lent to govt. of Victoria and N. S. Wales in 1883; and in 1884, on retirement from the army, became military adviser to the agts.-gen. of Victoria, N. S. Wales, Queensland, S. Australia, N. Zealand, and Tasmania.
STEWARD, GEORGE.—Cik., Tasmanian govt. rlyws., June, 1892; ch. cik. and acctnt., education dept., July, 1893; sec. to premier of Tasmania, Aug., 1894; cik. to ex. coun., Jan., 1896; and sec. to defence comte., June, 1896; in addition; under sec. for Tasmania, Jan., 1896; and ch. inspr. of explosives and magazines, 1st Sept., 1897, in addition; raised and commanded first company of mtd. infantry in Tasmania, and holds rank of captain; ch. cik., dept. of external affairs, Commonwealth govt., 18th May, 1901; offl. sec. to gov.-gen., and sec. to fed. ex. coun., 24th Dec., 1902.

STEWART, A.—Res. mag., Victoria E., Cape Col., Jan., 1882; transf. to Albert, 1884.

STEWART, JOHN MARCUS.—Cik., pol. ct., Queensland, 1887; ditto, pol. dept., 1888; sec., pol. investm. bd., 1889; acctnt., pol. dept., 1889; sub-lieut. in Queensland and Commonwealth of Aust. naval forces, 1st Nov., 1899, to 31st Jan., 1904; asst. treas., N. Nigeria, 6th Aug., 1904.

STEWART, MAJ.-GEN. SIR ROBERT MACGREGOR, K.C.B. (1902).—B. 1842; served in Hazara campaign, 1868; Afghan war, 1878-9; Soudan, 1885; A.D.C. to Queen Victoria, 1887-97; late commdr., R.A., south dist., Portmouth; gov. Bermuda, 19th Mar., 1904.

STIGAND, ALMAR GORDON.—2nd cik. to res. comsnr. for Bech. Prot. at Mafeking, 1898; 1st cik. and regiar. to res. comsnr., 1899; served in town guard during siege of Mafeking, Oct., 1899, to May, 1900; cik. of ct. and cik. to asst. comsnr., Gaberonesa, 1902; J.P., Bech. Prot., 1903; ag. asst. comsnr., Jan. to Feb., 1904.

STILES, ALFRED.—Apptd., after exam., messenger C.O., Dec., 1875; Queen's mess., Aug., 1882; asst. off. keeper, 17th Feb., 1900.

STILWELL, E. R.—Sarawak civ. ser., roads and bridges dept., Mar., 1888; asst. res., Baram, Oct., 1894; of Sadong, May, 1896; res., 2nd class, Jan., 1897; ditto, Bau, Upper Sarawak, 15th Oct., 1900.

STIRLING, SIR JOHN LANCELOT, KT. BACH. (1902), B.A., LL.B.—B. 1849; mem. leg. coun., S. Aust., 1891; chief sec., 1899; pres. leg. coun., 1901.

STIRLING, RIGHT REV. W. H., D.D.—Bishop of the Falklands.

STOKER, WILLIAM HENRY, K.C.—Called to the bar, Mid. Temp.; atty.-gen., Leeward Is., Mar., 1898; mem. fed. and island ex. and leg. comsrs.; ag. 1st puisne judge conjointly with atty.-gen., Nov. to Dec., 1901; atty.-gen., Barbados, July, 1902; chrmn., Barbados quarantine comsn., 1902-3; K.C., Barbados, 3rd April, 1903; M.L.C., Apl. to Oct., 1903; ag. pres. of educn. bd., May to June, 1903; ag. ch. just., 1st Aug. to 30th Oct., 1903; deleg. for Barbados, and elec. pres. at Brit. W. India conf. on quarantine, Apl. to May, 1904.

STONE, SIR E. A., KT. BACH. (1902).—B. 1844; cik. to atty.-gen., W. Australia, 1860; called to bar, 1865; cik. to legis. coun., 1870; nominee mem. of ditto, 1880-2; crown solr., 1882; puisne judge, 1884; acted as ch. just., 1880, 1881, 1887, and 1889; ch. just., 1901; admstr., 1901-2.

STONE, E. C. M.—Cik. to regiar., Trinidad, 1876; ch. clk., 1878; cik. of complaint ct., 1878; ch. clk. to regiar., sup. ct., 1880; regiar., ct. of survey, 1883; ag. regiar. sup. ct., 1880, 1881, 1883, and Apr., 1884, to July, 1885, and June to Sept., 1886; ch. clk. to regiar.-gen., Sept., 1887; dep. regiar.-gen., Oct., 1889; ag. regiar.-gen., 1892-93; is a comsnr. of affidavits, and supt. regiar. of births and deaths for Port of Spain.

STONE, HERBERT C.—Entered Trinidad service, Apr., 1863; asst. cik. of the peace, Port of Spain, May, 1864; ag. cik. of the peace, W. dist., co. of St. Patrick, July, 1865; 3rd cik., immigr. office, Mar., 1866; 2nd cik., June, 1867; ag. ch. cik., 1868-9; ag. stip. mag., co. of St. David's, and ward of Blanchisseuse, and warden of the Toco ward union, Feb., 1872; inspr. of imigrts., Nov., 1872; ag. warden and supervisor of the Caroni ward union, Feb., 1876; J.P. for the town of Port of Spain and counties of St. George and Caroni, May, 1876; inspr. and sub-prot. of imigrts., 1st Jan., 1882; ag. prot. of imigrts., 1882, 1887, and 1889-92, with seat in legis. coun.; mem. bd. of educn., June, 1892; ag. rec.-gen., with seat in legis. coun., 1892.

STOUT, THE HON. SIR ROBERT, K.C.M.G. (1886).—B. 1844; admitted a barrister of sup. ct., N. Zealand; entered the prov. coun. of Otago, N.Z., 1872; prov. solr., 1873; elected to the gen. assem., 1875; atty.-gen., Mar., 1878, to June, 1879; min. of lands, etc., for imigr., 1878; pres. of Dunedin Freethought Soc.; prime min. and atty.-gen., and min. for educn., 1884-87; fellow of N. Z. Univ.; chief justice of N.Z., 1899.

STRACHAN, W. HENRY W., C.M.G. (1902), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), F.L.S.—Jun. res. med. offr., pub. hosps., Kingston, Jamaica, 1882; sen. res. med. offr., 1885; sen. med. offr., 1892; mem. of bd. of govrns., Inst. of Jamaica, 1892; chief med. offr. of Lagos, Dec., 1897; acted as col sec., Dec., 1899, to Mar., 1900.

STRACHEY, CHARLES.—Apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. jun. cik., F.O., 2nd Apr., 1885; 1st cl. jun. cik., 1st May, 1885; sec. Uganda ry. comte., 10th Sept., 1896; 1st cl. cik., C.O., 20th Nov., 1898.

STRANGE, WM. LUMSDEN, M.I.C.E.—Served in pub. wks. dept., India, 1879 to 1903; under-sec., ditto, July, 1901; dir. of irrigtn. and water supply, Transvaal, 25th Apl., 1903; author of "Indian storage reservoirs with earthen drains."

STRATHCONA AND MOUNT ROYAL, LORD, 1ST BARON (U.K. creat. 1897), SIR DONALD A. SMITH, G.C.M.G. (1896), K.C.M.G. (1886).—B. 1820; Gov. of Hudson's Bay Territory; special comsnr., Red River, 1869; mem. of Canadian parlmt., 1871, dir. of Canadian Pacific Rly., 1880; high comsnr. for Canada, 1896; mem. of Pacific Cable Comtees., 1896 and 1899; Lord Rector of Aberdeen Univ., 1899.

STRATTON, GEORGE BERNARD.—Ed. Warwick and Durham Univ.; cadet, S. S., Nov., 1899; passed final exam. in Malay, Dec., 1900; ag. sup. govt. printing office, Jan., 1901; ag. 4th mag., Sing., Mar., 1901; ag. sup. of education, Penang, Dec., 1901; on spec. mission to Pulau Weh, Jan., 1904; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Apl., 1904; ag. sup. of educn., Penang, Nov., 1904; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Apr., 1905.

STRAWBRIDGE, WILLIAM, I.S.O. (1906).—Entered survey and crown lands dept., S. Australia, as cadet, June, 1862; after several promotions, was apptd. examr. of licensed survr.'s work and draftsman, June, 1872; and ch., draftsman, Apl., 1877; dep. survr.-gen., July, 1886; survr.-gen., July, 1894; chmn. of pastoral, central pastoral and central land bds.

STREATFEILD FRANK N., C.M.G. (1879).—B. 1843; comdt. of levies, S. Africa war, 1877-9; R.M. Transkei, 1878-84; C.C. Kuruman, B. Bech., 1887-9.

STRICKLAND, SIR GERALD, COUNT DELLA CATENA, K.C.M.G. (1897), C.M.G. (1889).—B. 1861; ed. Oscott Coll., Birmingham; lieut.
C.U.R.V., and elected mem. coun. of govt., Malta, 1886; B.A. and LL.B., Trin. Coll., Camb., honours law tripos; attended col. conf., 1887, on behalf of Malta; called to the bar, Inn. Temp., and pres. cholera comsn., Malta, 1887; thanked by govt. for negotiations on Imp. veto of appts. to see of Malta; unoffic. mem., ex. coun., and ag. ast. sec. to govt., 1888; vice-pres., bd. of health, pres., comttee. of privileges, ch. sec. to govt., and major, Royal Malta militia, which he established, 1889; re-organized Malta rwy., 1891; planned breakwater, 1894; pres., coun. of Malta univ., 1900; chrmn., mil. and civ. drainage bd.; mem. comttee. on Malta naval reserves; gov. and comdr.-in-chief, Leeward Is., 1902; estab. central factories for sugar and cotton in Antigua, 1903; gov., Tasmania, 23rd July, 1904.

STRIKLAND, R. B., M.A. (Dublin).—Inspr. of schools, Ceylon, 29th Aug., 1902.

STRONG, THE RT. HON. SIR SAMUEL HENRY, P.C. (1897), KT. BACH. (1893).—Born in Dorsetshire, Eng., 1825; called to bar of Ontario, 1849; created Q.C., 1863; elected a bencher of the Law Soc. of Upper Canada, 1860; a comnr. for consolidating the statutes of Upper Canada and Canada respectively, Dec., 1866; a mem. of the law reform comsn., 1871; vice-chancellor Ontario, Dec., 1869; puisne judge of the ct. of error and appeal, same prov., 1874; puisne judge of the sup. ct. of the Dominion, 1875; ch. just. of Canada, 1892; apptd. to the judicial comttee. of H.M.'s privy coun., 1897.

STROUD, BENJ.—Suptdng. srgt., Barbados; pol. supt., 1876; 3rd class landg. waiter, Sept., 1881.

STUART, ALEXR.—Ed. St. Andrew's Univ.; regir. of impts. and expts., Singapore, Sept., 1890; temporarily attached to patent office, London, 1897-8.

STUART, JAMES.—Ed. St. John's Coll., Hurstpierpoint; matric. Lond. and Cape; silver medal, Natal, Eng. lit. exam., 1891; clk. G.P.O., Pietermaritzburg, Feb., 1888; clk. and interp., R.M., Eshowe, May, 1888; 1st clk. and interp. to res. comsnr. and ch. mag., Zululand, Feb., 1889; acted on various occasions as sec., res. comsnr. and res. ch. mag.'s ct., Zululand; interp. to Br. comsnr., Swaziland, 1894 to 1895; and in charge of Swazi deputations to Capetown and England in 1894; acted as Br. consul, Swaziland, 1895; R.M., Ingavuma dist., Zululand, 1895; mag., Lower Tugela div., 1899; asst. mag., Durban div., 1901; mag. for colony, 1902.

STUART COL. JOHN ALEXANDER MAN, C.B. (Mil., 1900), C.M.G. (1897), KT. OF JUSTICE OF ST. JOHN OF JERUSALEM (1903).—B. 1841; served with the field force under the late Brigadier Murray, R.A.; employed on the 30-mile radius round Shanghai during the summer of 1863 (medal); also with the Anglo-Chinese contingent in Col. Gordon's Taeping campaigns of 1863-64, being present during the operations before Soo-chow, and at the siege and storming of Chang-chow (Chinese medal and Precious Star 2nd class); in 1868-69 was stationed in Formosa, and assisted the U.S. Consul and Mr. W.A. Pickering, C.M.G., in concluding a friendly settlement with the savage tribes; took part in the negotiations at Fort Zelandia and withdrawal of Br. force (mentioned in despatches); selected in 1873 to raise a corps of mil. pol. for the Treaty dist. of Newchwang, S. Manchuria, at that time infested by mounted banditti, and subsequently commanded the force embodied (thanks of the Br. and Ital. ministers, and of the Imp. High Comsnr., with the brevet of col. in the Chinese army, and the cross of the Ital. Crown, 4th class); served with the Nile expdn. of 1884-5 as boat offr. and staff. offr., and afterwards as comdt. at Dal (medal with clasp and Khedive's star); A.D.C. to Gen. Valentine Baker, Pasha, in 1888; and ag. dep. inspr.-gen. of gendarmerie in 1886-7-8 (thanks of Egyptian Govt., and Order of the Osmanieh, 4th class); comdt. of local forces, Trinidad and Tobago, 1891 to 1897; comdt. at base and on line of communication, Ashanti camp, 1900 (twice mentd. in desps., medal).

STUBBS, REGINALD EDWARD.—Ed. at Radley and Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford (exhibitioner); 1st cl. classical mods., 1897; 1st cl. lit. hum., 1899; B.A., 1899; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. clk., C.O., Jan., 1900.

SULLIVAN, ADMIRAL SIR FRANCIS W., BART., R.N., K.C.B. (1879), C.B. (1864), C.M.G. (1878).—B. 1834; entered the royal navy, 1848; comdr. of "Harrier" in N. Zealand, 1862-4, during Maori wars; presentat.Kohero, Raugariri and other minor affairs; promoted capt., 1863, and rear-admiral, 1878; commodore on the Cape and African station, 1877 to 1879, during operations in the Cape and Zululand; received the thanks of both houses of parlmt. for his services in connection with the Egyptian expdn., 1882; vice-admiral, 1885; dir. of transports, admiralty, 1883.

SULLIVAN, W. W., K.C.—Atty.-gen. and premier of Prince Edward Is., Canada; born in P.E.I., 1843; called to the bar 1867; elected to legislature in 1872, and has continuously represented the same constituency; created a Q.C. by the govt. of P.E.I., 1876, and by the gov.-gen. of Canada 1879; is a dep. judge in the admity., cl., pres. of the bd. of educn., and pres. of the bd. of trustees of P.E.I. Hosp. for the Insane; was a mem. of the exec. coun., holding the office of solr.-gen., Apr., 1873, till Sept., 1876; leader of the Opposition in the legislature in 1877; became prime min. and atty. and advoc.-gen. in 1879, which position he continues to hold; has been a deleg. representing the prov. govt. on several occasions in Canada, and was a deleg. to England in 1886, to confer with the impl. govt. regarding the terms of confederation between P.E.I. and Canada; ch. just., P.E.I., 1889.

SUTER, WM. CHAS.—Asst. master, govt. English schla., Singapore, 22nd Nov., 1884; ch. clk., col. sec.'s office, 1st July, 1888; shorthand reporter to leg. coun. in addition to other duties, 1st July, 1897.

SUTHERLAND, WM.—Apptd. to Fiji civ. ser., Jan., 1880; clk. recr.-gen.'s office, Sept., 1880; clk., registr.-gen., Jan., 1882; stip. mag. of the col., Apl., 1883; ag. collr. of cust., Sept., 1897; ag. recr.-gen., Mar., 1898; native comsnr., 1898; ag. col. sec. and recr.-gen., Jan., 1903.

SUTTOR, THE HON. SIR FRANCIS B., KT. BACH. (1903).—Postmr.-gen., N.S. Wales, Aug., 1890, to Nov., 1891; min. of pub. instruction, 1891 to 1893, and again, 1891-4; represntve. of col. at col. confce., Ottawa, 1894.

SWAIN, ALFRED WILLIAM.—Clerical asst., regir.'s off., Barbados, 1879; Jun. clk., G.P.O., Br. Guiana, June, 1881; 3rd cls. clk., Jan., 1883; 2nd cls., Dec., 1889; 1st cls., Apr., 1900; ch. clk., Sept., 1900; ag. postmr.-gen., May, 1901, to May, 1902; and Aug. to Dec. 1904; 2nd lieut. Br. Guiana volunteers, 1889, ditto militia, 1891; lieut., 1892; capt., 1895; maj., 1900; ag. comdt. of local forces, July, 1901, to Feb. 1902; Hythe certif., 1898; Colonial and Aux. forces long service medal; recd. thanks of govt. on retiring in 1902, and retains rank of Major.
SWAIN, ARTHUR CLAUDE.—2nd clk., crown lands dept., Br. Guiana, Oct., 1879; asst. comsry., May, 1882; dist. ditto, July, 1881; is a J.P.

SWAIN, GEORGE DOUGLAS.—1st clk. and bookkeeper, pol dept., Br. Guiana, Apr., 1882; inspr. of pol., May, 1884; ch. inspr., Mar., 1892; ag. dep. inspr.-gen., July to Sept., 1893; on special service with Mr. McTurk, Feb., 1895, to take over Uruan from Venezuelans, remaining in command there till July, 1895; volr. in Ashanti expedn., Nov., 1895, to Mar., 1896; mentioned in despatches (star); two months' training with R.I.C. at Dublin, 1890; Hythe, P.S., and 1st cl. ambulance certifa.; ag. dep. inspr.-gen., Aug., 1898, to Jan., 1899; promoted ch. county inspr., and 2nd in command, 18th Nov., 1899; ag. insp.-gen., 10th May to 21st Aug., 1900; servd. on comsn. apptd. to inquire into admstrn. of poor law relief, 1900; ag. inspr.-gen. of police, and col. commt. of militia, 8th May to 3rd Sept., 1902; deputy inspr.-gen. of police, Trinidad, 30th September, 1903.

SWAMY, PONNAMBALAM COOMARA.—Mem. legis. coun., Ceylon, and mun. coun., Colombo; proctor, sup. ct., and notary public; served on comsn. to inquire into and report on financial condition of Colombo municipality.

SWAN, ROBERT A.—Matric. at Madras Univ., Dec., 1868; passed special law test prescribed for uncoventional supts. and asst. supts. ofpol.; 2nd class inspr. of pol. in the Cuddapah dist., Madras, May, 1870; in Aug., 1871, 1st class; May, 1874, passed in Telugu; Oct., 1876, special asst. to sub-collr. and joint mag. of Cuddapah for famine relief duty, and in same month apptd. mag., and placed in charge of the Kadri and Madnapully Taluqs of Cuddapah dist.; in Feb., 1877, stip. mag. Mauritius; Jan., 1878, stip. mag. of Faloq; and in Aug., 1879, Grand Port and Savanne; mem. of comsn. to frame regulae under "labour ordinance of 1878"; member of Lincoln's Inn, 1882; called to the bar, 1887; stip. mag. Br. Guiana, Nov., 1883; in July, 1884, sent on special duty to Madras to organise an emigr. agency for Br. Guiana; sheriff, Essequibo co., Dec., 1887; chinm. lands titles inquiry comsn., Feb., 1890; a revising barrister under Br. Guiana Constit. Order, 1891; sheriff of Berbice and mag. New Amsterdam, 1892; acted as pol. mag. Georgetown, Feb., 1890, and Oct., 1894, to Apr., 1895; mem. of comsn. on poor-relief, 6th Apr., 1900; chairman of ditto, 7th Sept., 1900; appt. as pol. mag. Georgetown, confirmed by S. of S., 1st Oct., 1900; ag. puisne judge, sup. ct., 1st Oct., 1900; puisne judge, Trinidad, 3rd Aug., 1903.

SWANN, ALFRED JAMES.—Employed in contracting treaties with chiefs north of Lake Tanganyika on behalf of British govt., and recd. thanks of Lord Salisbury, 1893; apptd. collr. of revs., Br. Cent. Africa Prot., 1894; in charge of expdn. against Mwasi and Saidi Kasungu, 1895 (Br. Cent. Africa medal); judicial offr., 1896; 1st cls. asst., 1899; Br. comsnr. to the Anglo-Portuguese boundary delimitation, 1899; has recd. Royal Humane Soc. silver medal for saving life in Lake Nyasa.

SWAYNE, CHARLES RICHARD.—Stip. mag., Fiji; inspr. of native taxes, 1876; stip. mag. and comsnr. of sup. ct., Lau prov., 1878; sent to Kadava with special authority in native matters, 1879 and 1880; inspr. of Indian and Polynesian labourers, Lau prov., 1883; stip. mag., regiar., and comsnr. of sup. ct. at Levuka, 1885; returned to Lau, 1886; asst. native comsnr., Lau, 1888; ag. Br. res., Gilbert and Ellice Is., and special judicial comsnr. for trial of certain cases, Oct., 1893, to Nov., 1895; stip. mag., Rewa, and comsnr., Naitasiri, 1893; ag. native comsnr., and mem. exec. coun., 29th July, 1901, to 11th Sept., 1902; comsnr. Naitasiri, Sept., 1902; ag. comsnr., Rewa, 27th May to 31st Dec., 1903; offl. mem. leg. coun., 7th Apr., 1906.

SWAYNE, BRIG.-GEN. ERIC JOHN EAGLES, C.B.—Joined Indian staff corps; entd. army, 1883; served in Burmah, 1886-87 (medal with clasp); spec. duty, Somaliland reconnaissence, 1890-92; served Uganda Mutiny and Jubaland, 1898 (medal with clasp); commanded Somaliland field force, 1901-2 and 1902-3 (brevet, medal and clasp); O.C. troops, Somaliland, 1904, with local rank brig.-gen.; intell. branch, headqrs., India, 1902-3 (McGregor medallist); comsnr., comdr.-in-chief and consul-gen., Somaliland Prot., 1st Mar., 1902; comsnr. and comdr.-in-chief, ditto, 23rd June, 1904.

SWEET-ESCOTT, SIR E. B., K.C.M.G. (1904), C.M.G. (1895).—B. 1857; ed. Somersetshire Coll., Bath, and at Balliol Coll., Oxon; exhibitioner, Worce. Coll., Oxon, June 1876; 2nd class classical moda., June, 1878; 3rd class in mod. hist. finals, June, 1880; B.A., July, 1880; classical prof. at the Roy. Coll., Mauritius, June, 1881; précis writer, col. sec.'s office, Feb., and 2nd ast. col. sec., Apl., 1886; ag. col. sec., 1889; ag. col. sec., Br. Honduras, Mar., 1893; admstd. the govt. of that col., Apr. to Nov., 1893; col. sec., Br. Honduras, 1894; admstd. govt. Apl. to Nov., 1895, again in 1897; ag. 1st class clk., C.O., Jan., 1898; admstr. of the Seychelles Is., Aug., 1899; assumed govt., 20th Nov., 1899; gov. and comdr-in-chief, Oct., 1903; gov., B. Honduras. 15th Apl., 1904.

SWETTENHAM, SIR F. ATHELSTANE, K.C.M.G.(1897), C.M.G.(1886).—B.1850; cadet, S. Stilts., July, 1870; passed final exam. in Malay, July, 1872; asst. collr. of land rev. for Penang and Prov. Wellesley, Aug., 1872; collr. of land rev., July, 1873; J.P. and mag. and comsnr., ct. of requests, Penang, May, 1874; sent on special missions to Perak in Jan., June, and July, 1874; sent to reside with the Sultan of Selangor, Aug., 1874; asst. res., Selangor, Dec., 1874; gazetted to act temporarily as res. of Selangor, 22nd Oct., 1875; took charge of the residency in Perak on the murder of the res., Nov., 1875; dep. comsnr., Perak, Nov., 1875; mentioned in despatches; asst. col. sec. for native states, Mar., 1876; asst. col. sec., July, 1881; Br. res., Selangor, Sept., 1882; comsnr. for S. S. and Malay States, Calcutta Exhibn., 1883-84; ag. Br. res. Perak, Mar., 1884, to Jan., 1886; exec. comsnr. for S. S. and Malay States, Col. and Ind. Exhibn., 1886; Br. res., Perak, 1889; res.-gen. Malay States, Jan., 1896; admstd. govt. S. S., Feb., 1900; gov., 1901; ret. 1904.

SWETTENHAM, SIR J. A., K.C.M.G. (1898), C.M.G. (1892).—B. 1846; ed. Clare Coll., Camb.; scholarship, May, 1867; writer, Ceylon service, 1868; ag. pol. mag., Harrispattu, Feb., 1870; pol. mag., Kayts, Sept., 1870, continuing to act at Harrispattu; ag. asst. govt. agt., Galle, Dec., 1871; ag. landing and tide survr., Galle, June, 1872; asst. collr. of customs, Jaffna, Oct., 1872, to continue to act at Galle; ag. dist. judge, Matara, Apr., 1873; 2nd ast. col. sec., and clk. of the legis. coun., 1876; rec.-gen., Cyprus, 1883; audr.-gen., Ceylon, 1891; col. sec., S. S., 1896; admstd. govt., June to Aug., 1895, from Mar. to Dec., 1898, and from Dec., 1899, to Feb., 1901; gov. Br. Guiana, 1901; gov., Jamaica, 14th July, 1904.

SYDNEY, BISHOP OF (AUSTRALIA, METROPOLITAN AND PRIMATE OF) (Bishopric founded
1847). MOST REV. W. SAUMAREZ SMITH, D.D.—Consec., 1890.

SYMONT, SIR JOSIAH HENRY.—K.C.M.G. (1901); K.C.; mem. of H. of Ass., S. Australia, 1881-1887; atty.-gen., 1881; Q.C. 1881; representative to Aus. fed. conv., 1897-8, and chmn. of its judiciary comttee.; pres. of fed. league of S. Aust.; pres. of Commonwealth league; mem. of univ. coun.; senr. for S. Aust., Commonw. parl., Mar., 1901; atty.-gen., ditto, Oct., 1904; atty.-gen., Commonw., 1904-5.

SYMONDS, J. D. T.—Served in different regts. of Lancers, 1876-90; asst. inspr., G. coast constab., Mar., 1890; asst. supt. of pol., S. S., 1891.

TAIT, ALFRED.—Supernumerary clk., Trinidad, Mar., 1889; extra clk., savings bank dept., 1st Sept., 1890; 3rd clk., royal gaol off., 1st Jan., 1891; 3rd clk., educn. off., Apr., 1891; 3rd asst. clk. of the peace, for Sup. of-Prin., 1st June, 1891; 4th clk., col. sec.'s off., 12th July, 1892; 3rd clk., col. sec.'s off., 16th Aug., 1897; ag. ch. clk., col. sec.'s off., and clk. to leg. coun., Nov., 1897; June, 1897; Nov., 1898; and Nov., 1900; sec. to the col. coun.; priv. sec. to Govr. Sir F. Napier Broome; sec. to the municipal inquiry comsn., 1896; clerical asst. to comsn. apptd. to inquire into admn. of just. in Trinidad; sec. to industrial educn. comsn.; priv. sec. to Sir H. E. H. Jerningham.

TALBOT, MAJ.-GEN. HON. SIR REGINALD ARTHUR JAMES.—K.C.B. (1902); C.B. (1885); b. 1841; ed. Harrow; formerly A.D.C. to Queen Victoria; M.P. for Stafford, 1869-74; serv. in Zulu War, 1879; Egyptian Campaign, 1882; Nile expdn., 1884-85; lt.-col. 1st Life Guards, 1886-88; mil. attache, Paris, 1889-95; comg. cavly. brig., Aldershot, 1896-99; comd. army of occupation, Egypt, 1899-1903; gov. of Victoria, 16th Feb., 1904.

TALMA, EDWY L.—B.A. Christ's Coll., Camb., 14th Wrangler, Math. tripus, 1895; cadet, S. S., Nov., 1890; ag. asst. prot. immgrts., Penang, Aug., 1897, to Mar., 1898; and from Oct., 1898; confirmed Jan., 1901; passed final exam. in Tamil, Feb., 1889; ag. asst. P.M.G., Penang, Apr., 1902; ag. 3rd mag., Penang, May, 1903; ag. 2nd ditto, Nov., 1903; asst. supt. of Indian immgrts., in addition to other duties, Nov., 1903; dep. registr., sup. ct. Singapore, July, 1904.

TANNER, J. E., M.I.C.E., C.M.G. (1894).—B.1834; ed. at the Coll. for Civ. Engrs., Putney; pupil to Messrs. James and William Simpson, and to Mr. (afterwards Sir) Charles Hutton Gregory, on the Graisissac rly., in the Cevennes, France; joined the army works corps before Sebastopol as asst. supt., 1855; and served with the force until the peace, 1856; asst. engr., on the Ind. Guaranteed rly., (Scinde and Punjab), 1856; mem. of the Anarkulle European volrs. throughout the Ind. mutiny; dist. engr., 1858; and engr. in-charge of the Sutlej div., Delhi rly., including the Sutlej bridge, 1862; apptd. to survey for a rly. in Trinidad, 1871; and to superintend its construction, 1873; dir. of pub. wks. and gen. supt. of rlys., 1875; M.L.C., 1886; ret., 1894.

TARTE, HON. J. ISRAEL.—A notary by profession, but only practised two years; editor of Le Canadien since 1874; sat in the legis. assem. of Quebec, Feb., 1887, to Dec., 1891; first returned to parlmt. in 1891, and again in 1896; min. of pub. wks. in Sir W. Laurier's govt., 1896-1902.

TASCHEREAU, RIGHT HON. SIR H. E., KT. BACH. (1902), K.C., LL.D., P.C. (1904).—B. 1836; puisne judge, sup. ct., Quebec, 1871; puisne judge, supreme ct. of Canada, 1878; ch. just. of Canada, 1902.

TAUBMAN-GOLDIE, P.C. (1898), THE RT. HON. SIR GEORGE DASHWOOD, K.C.M.G. (1887).—B. 1846; founder and dep. chmn. of the Royal Niger Co.; chmn., 1895.

TAYLOR, A. W. FORBES.—4th clk., treas., Natal, June, 1878; 3rd clk., Apr., 1879; 2nd clk., July, 1881; 1st clk., audit office, Mar., 1884; inspr., audit dept., 1897; ch. inspr., 1903.

TAYLOR, FRANK.—Architectural asst., P. W. D., Cape Town, 3rd Nov., 1900, to 8th Jan., 1901; on active serv., lieut. in irregular corps, 8th Jan., 1901, to 7th Apr., 1902; chief draughtsman, P. W. D., O. R. C., 18th Apr., 1902.

TAYLOR, JOHN.—Entd. Royal Navy, 1883; served in Soudan war, 1884-5 (Medal and Khedive's bronze star); warder, Pentonville prison, Lond., Dec., 1887, to June, 1897; ch. warder, Belize pris., B. Hond., July, 1897; keeper of prisons, 1898; ag. dist. comsnr., Toledo, 1st Apr. to 5th Sept., 1905.

TAYLOR, BANIL R. H., F.R.A.S.—En. R.N. 1878; served in Egyptian war, 1882 (medal and clasp, Khedive's bronze star); lieut., 1888; served on Mediterranean, N. America, and W. India, China, and home stations; res. comsn., 1898; asst. harbmr., Hong Kong, July, 1899; ag. harbmr., Mar., 1900, to June, 1901, Sept., 1903, to Feb., 1904, and Aug. to Nov., 1905; M.L.C., June, 1900, to June, 1901, Sept., 1903, to Feb., 1904, and Aug. to Nov., 1905; ag. A.S.P. in addition, Oct., 1904.

TAYLOR, SIR W. T., K.C.M.G. (1905), C.M.G. (1895).—B. 1848; collr. of customs and excise, Larnaca, 1879; ch. collr. of customs, Cyprus, 1882; ag. recvr.-gen., Nov., 1883, to Feb., 1884; ag. comsnr., Larnaca, in addition to his own duties, 1883 and 1885; ag. recvr.-gen., in addition to duties as ch. collr. of cust., Jan. to Nov., 1887; recvr.-gen. and ch. collr. of cust. and excise, 1891; audr.-gen., Ceylon, May, 1895; ag. col. sec., Ceylon, Oct., 1895, to Feb., 1896, Mar. to Dec., 1896, Mar. to Nov., 1899, and Apl., 1900, to Nov., 1901; col. sec., S. Setttmbs., June, 1901; admntd. gov't. of S. S., Oct., 1903, to Apl., 1904; ag. res.-gen., F.M.S., Sept., 1904; confirmed, Jan., 1905.

TEMPANY, HAROLD A.—B.So. (Lond.), A.I.C.; asst. agric. chemist, Leeward Is., 1903.

TEMPLER, FREDERIC GORDON.—Ed. at Harrow and at Trin. Coll., Camb.; called to the bar, Inn. Temp., Nov., 1872; went the W. circuit; apptd. dist. judge, Kyrenia, Cyprus, 1882; ag. puisne judge, sup. ct., May to Oct., 1888; Nov., 1888, to Feb., 1889; Jan. to Mar., 1890; and May to Sept., 1891; dist. judge, Larnaca, 1891; Queen's advoc., Cyprus, 1893; countct. judge, York, 1893.

TEMPLER, John Harvey, B.A.—Office asst. to atty.-gen., Ceylon, 13th Jan., 1881; crown counsel, 24th Sept., 1892; has acted as dist. judge, atty.-gen., and solr.-gen. on several occasions.

TENNANT, HERCULES.—Barrister-at-law, Inn. Tem.; advoc., sup. ct., Cape col., 1873; sec. of law comsn., 1879; represented Caledon in house of assem., 1879-81; lieut., D.E.O.V.R., 1878-81; extra A.D.C. to gov. and comdr.-in-chief, July, 1879; served in Basuto war, 1880-81 (medal), with rank of capt., as asst. staff offr. to Gen. Clarke, C.B., and afterwards to Col. Carrington, C.M.G.; sec. to ch. just., 1882; librarian of the sup. ct., 1882; asst. registr., sup. ct., and official reviser of authorised edition of Cape statutes, 1884; asst.
COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.

registr., ct. of appeal, Mar., 1886; J.P. for Cape-
town and dist., and Capt. dist., July, 1886; ag.
taxing offr., sup. ct., Sept., 1884, and Aug. to
Dec., 1885; Apr. and Oct., 1886; Mar. and June,
1887; and Oct., 1887, to Jan., 1889; taxing offr.,
Feb., 1889; high sheriff, Oct., 1889; regis. of
sup. ct., 1894; sec. to law dept., Transvaal, 1st
June, 1901; J.P., 1901; advocate of sup. ct.,
1902; examiner of candidates for admission as
conveyancers, 1902; editor and compiler of "The
Notary's Manual"; "The Justice of the Peace's
Manual"; "Rules of Court"; "Chronological
Table and Index of the Statute Law of the Colony,
1714-1883"; "Masters and Servants Laws of the
Colony"; joint editor (by authority) of a revised
edition of "The Cape Statutes, 1652-1886, and
of the Griqualand W. Statutes"; also compiled
(under authority), "The Index of Government
Proclamations and Notices, 1803-1881."

TENNYSON, Rt. Hon. Lord, 2nd Baron
(U.K.), creat. 1884), G.C.M.G. (1903), K.C.M.G.
(1899). HALLAM TENNYSON, succeeded 1892 (on
the death of his father), Alfred Lord Tennyson,
poet laureate, 1850-92.—B. 1852; ed. Marl. Coll.,
Trin. Coll., Camb., and Inner Temple; J.P. for
Hants; mem. of Marl. Coll. exec. coun.; pre-
pared his father's memoir, published in 1897; gov.
S. Australia, 1899; gov.-gen., Commonwealth of
Australia, 1902-1904.

THOMAS, E. J.—Entered Victoria service,
1852; receiver of revenue, etc., 1863; acted as
sec. to numerous boards and comms.; priv. sec.
to Sir B. O'Loughlen, Bart., 1881; sec., premier's
dept., 1883.

THOMPSON, ALFRED.—Apptd., after exam.,
3rd cl. messenger, C.O., May, 1880; 2nd cl., July,
1891.

THOMPSON, AUGUSTUS WM.—Asst. clk. of ct.,
G. Coast, 1873; clk. to Queen's advoc., 1874-5;
dep. registr., cent. prov., 1877; ch. registr., 1880;
postmr., Cape Coast, Mar. to Aug., 1884; registr.
and interp., W. Prov., 1884; registr. of deeds and
taxing master, W. Prov.; diar. comanr., G. C.
col., May, 1889.

THOMPSON, JAR., M.I.C.E.—Entd. Queen's
Coll., Cork, 1879; B.E., Roy. Univ. of Ireland,
1882; pupil at pub. wks. and docks bd., Dublin,
1882-3; asst. engrnr., Southport and Cheshire lines
extension rly., 1883-84; asst. engrnr., survey,
design, etc., Cavan, Leitrim and Roscommon light
rly., 1884-85; res. engrnr., construction of rlys.
and harb. wks., Ireland, 1885-89; draftsman and
asst. survr., Victorian rlys., 1889-91; asst. engrnr.,
P.W.D., W. Australia, 1891-93; res. engrnr.,
Yilgarn rly., May, 1893; dist. engrnr., Nov., 1895;
engnr.-in-charge of rly. constn., June, 1896;
engnr.-in-charge of harb. and rivers (in addition
to rly. construction), Aug., 1896; inspctg. engrnr.,
July, 1902; ag. engrnr.-in-chief, Mar., 1904;
engnr.-in-chief and consulting engrnr. to the
Freemantle Harb. Trust, Sept., 1904.

THOMPSON, JOHN.—Ent. Royal Irish con-
stab., Belfast, 1864 to 1870; obtained apptm. in
the convict ser., Woking, England; asst. in re-
forming prison ser. in Jamaica, Oct., 1883; prin.
warder and storekr., gen. penitentiary, to July,
1888, then dep. supt. of same; ag. supt. to Dec.,
1894; supt. of St. Catherine dist. prison, Spanish
Town, Jamaica, Nov., 1897.

THOMPSON, THOMAS AUGUSTUS.—Called to
bar, Oct., 1872; in Easter term, 1874, received
coman. to act as public prosecutor in the crim. ct.,
Bahamas; acted as judge of court of common pleas
from June to Dec., 1875; pol. mag., Bahamas
(being still allowed priv. practice), Jan., 1876;
chmn. of man. comtee. of prisons, and presides
over investigations into cases of wreck and other
marine casualty; mem. of the Bahamas legislature,
and trustee of the Nassau Museum and Library,
1881; stip and circuit mag., 1886; ag. atty.-gen.,
1887; ag. ch. just., July, 1890, June to Oct.,
1891, and June to Nov., 1892; ag. col. sec. and
chmn. of bd. of educ., Oct., 1890; judge and col.
sec., Falklands, 1893; admstd. govt., July to
Nov., 1894; regis. and marshal, sup. ct., Trinid.,
1897.

THOMPSON, WALTER.—Supt.'s astt., Sker-
rett's training schl., Leeward Is., June, 1892, to
Apr., 1894; 4th outdoor offr., treasy. dept., Apr.,
1894, to Jan., 1895; 3rd ditto, Jan., 1895, to
Dec., 1902; 2nd ditto, Dec., 1902, to Feb., 1903;
1st ditto, Feb., 1903; admeasurer of shipg., Nov.,
1903; ag. 1st indoor offr., treasy. dept., Dec.,
1903; ag. harbrmr., Feb., 1904; 1st outdoor offr.
and ag. harbrmr., May, 1904; appt. 1st outdoor
offr. and harbrmr. on the amalgamation of offices,
June, 1904.

THOMPSON, W. A.—2nd cl. supervsr. G.
Coast, Apr., 1894; ag. ast. treas., Cape Coast Castle,
Mar., 1895; cashr., Accra, Mar., 1896; ag. ast. treas.,
Apr., 1896; 1st cl. supervsr., Sept., 1897; sent on
serv. in hinterland, Feb., 1898; invalided and
retd from West Afr., Feb., 1900; treas., etc.,
Falklands, July, 1901; mem. exec. and legis.
couns.; ag. col. sec., May to Nov., 1902, and
Apl., 1903, to Jan., 1904.

THOMPSTONE, SYDNEY WILSON.—F.R.C.S.,
Edin., M.R.C.P., Edin., D.P.H., Camb.; form.
house surg., Roy. Infir., Glasgow; apptd. dist.
med. offr., Oil Riv. Protec. (now S. Niger.), Mar.,
22nd, 1893; asst. prin. med. offr., 1897; ag. prin.
med. offr., Aug.-Nov., 1898; Nov., 1899, to June,
1900, and June, 1901, to Oct., 1902; prin. med. offr.,
N. Nigeria, May, 1903.

THOMSON, ALEX. MCDONALD.—Ed. Abdn.
Univ., M.A.; 1st class hon. math., 1883; asst.
prof. of math., Aberdeen, 1886-7; Bacon scholar,
Gray's Inn, 1888; cadet, Hong Kong, 1887;
passed cadet, Dec., 1890; ag. supt., Victoria
gaol, Apr., 1891, to Mar., 1892; ag. clk. of couns.,
Jan., 1891, to Oct., 1892; ag. astl. col. sec., Mar.
to Oct., 1892; ag. registr.-gen. and provisional
mem. exec. and legis. couns., 1893; ag. astl. col.
sec., 1894; ag. col. treas., Mar., 1895; and pro-
visional mem. exec. and legis. couns.; mem.
governing body of Queen's Coll., 1894;
postmr.-gen., 1897; col. treas., 1898; mem.
exec. and legis. couns., 1899; ag. col. sec., Apr.,
1902; and Nov., 1903, to July, 1904.

THOMSON, HON. DUGALD.—Mem. Leg. Ass.,
New South Wales, 1894, 1895, and 1898; mem.
of Commonw. parl., Mar., 1901, and Dec., 1903;
min. for home affairs, ditto, Oct., 1904.

THOMSON, JOHN CHRISTOPHER.—Ed. Edin.
Univ.; M.D., 1892; M.B., C.M., with 2nd cl.
honours, 1888; M.A., 1884; Edin. Univ. cert.
in diseases of trop. climates, 1904; D.P.H. (Edin.
and Glas.), 1904; dip. in trop. med. and hygiene
(Camb.), 1904; formerly suptd. of Alice Memorial
hosp. and Nethersole hosp., Hong Kong; hon.
sec. and lecturer on tropical diseases, Hong
Kong Coll. of med. for Chinese; ent. Hong Kong
civil service, med. dept., Jan., 1897; gaol surg.,
med. offr. in charge of infective diseases hospital,
and inspctg. med. offr. of Tung Wah hosp.; J.P.,
1898; pres. Hong Kong and China branch of Br.
med. assocnt., 1899; also med. offr. in charge of
post-mortem exams., 1897 to 1901; med. offr. in
charge of Victoria hosp. for women and children,
1905.
THOMSON, JOHN HASTINGS.—Ed. Wallace Hall Academy, Dumfries-shire, Scotland; apptd. asst. dist. offr., Somaliland, May, 1901; ag. consul, Berbera, Sept., 1901, to Aug., 1903; ag. dist. offr., Bulhar, Jan., 1904-5; polit. offr. with Gen. Swayne in Abyssinia, Mar. to Apr., 1905; polit. offr. with troops on Abyssinian border, May to July, 1905; ag. sub-comsnr., Zeyla, 2nd June, 1905.

THORBURN, HON. SIR ROBERT, K.C.M.G. (1887).—Emig. to Newfoundland, 1852, where he has been engaged in mercantile pursuits; M.I.C., 1870; premier, 1885; deleg. to col. confce., 1887; defeated at gen. election, 1889, and resig. office.

THORBURN, J. JAMIESON.—Writer, Ceylon, Oct., 1886; ag. govt. atty., N. cent. prov., Mar. to Aug., 1889; ag. pol. mag., Galle, Dec., 1893; ag. off. asst. to govt. agts. in various dists. from Oct., 1893, to 1895; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Jan., 1896; 2nd asst. col. sec., Jan. and Dec., 1898, and June, 1899; ag. asst. postmr.-gen., Jan., 1899; 2nd asst. col. sec., June, 1899; ag. sec. central irrigation board, Jan., 1900; principal asst. col. sec. and joint sec., loan board, May, 1900; senior prov. comsnr. (in anticipation of proposed amalgamation of the admstns. of Lagos and S. Nigeria), performed duties of sec. to admstrn. of S. Nigeria, dep. high comsnr., S. Nigeria, Mar. to June, 1905; ag. gov't., Lagos, and ag. high comsnr., S. Nigeria, July, 1905.

THORNTON, RIGHT REV. SAMUEL, D.D., 1ST BISHOP OF BALLARAT, VICTORIA.—Consec. 1875; scholar and fellow, Queen's Coll., Oxon; B.A., 1856; incumbent of St. Jude's, Whitechapel, 1860; rector of St. George's, Birmingham, 1864.

THORNTON, SWINFORD LESLIE, R.A.—Lincoln Coll., Oxn; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn Nov., 1877; admitted to the bar, S. Settlements, Nov., 1886; regis., sup. ct.; comsnr., ct. of requests and collr. of stamps, Malacca, June, 1887; ag. sen. mag., Singapore, July, 1888; regis., sup. ct. and mag., Malacca, July, 1892; atty.-gen., St. Vincent 1894; ag. admstr., Nov., 1894, to Mar., 1895; ag. ch. just., Nov., 1895; res. mag., Jamaica, 1896; mem. comttee. to revise rules and form res. mag. cts., 1897; mem. parochial bds. comn.; and chirrn. house and land tax comtce., 1899; ag. puisne judge, 1901; puisne judge, S. Sttltns., 22nd Mar., 1904.

THORPE, WM. EDWARD.—Offr., cls. III., Ceylon civ. ser.; ed. St. Edmund's Sch., Canterbury; cadet, Ceylon, 1891; office asst., Anuradhapura, 1892; ditto, Jaffna, 1894; ditto, Ratnapura, 1896; ditto, Colombo, 1896, with additional duties as asst. supt. pol.; asst. govt. agt., Kalutara, 1898; ditto, Chilaw, 1899; dist. judge, Matara, 1900; pol. mag., Colombo, 1903; dep. collr. cust., Colombo, 1905.

TIBBITS, A. C. K.—Employed col. sec.'s off.; treas. and aud. off., Antigua, Apr. to Dec., 1894; clk. sav. bank, Jan., 1895; 1st clk., post off., Jan., 1898; ag. postmr. in 1899, 1900, 1901, 1903, 1904 and 1905.

TICE, W. G.—Apptd., after exam., 3rd cl. mess., C.O., 19th Feb., 1900; 2nd cl., 1st Feb., 1902.

TILLARD, RICHARD.—Twenty years service under Cape govt.; was R.M. and collr. of customs, Port Nolloth, when he retired in 1875; road mag. and J.P. for the several dists. of Cape Col.; served as an offr. of volrs. in the Gaika and Basuto wars; Kafr war medal, 1877-8; R.M., Mafeking, Jan., 1886; C.C., Dec., 1886; supt. of tels., Br. Bechuana-land, Oct., 1886; R.M., Vryburg, 1889; civ. comsnr. and res. mag., Fort Beaufort, 10th May, 1898.

TIMPERLEY, WILLIAM HENRY.—Ed. at Shrewsbury Gram. Schl., Univ. Berne; entered W. Australian pol., 1856; inspr., 1870; supt. of Rottnest Is., 1885; R.M., Bunbury.

TODD, SIR CHARLES, M.A., K.C.M.G. (1893), C.M.G. (1872).—B. 1826; Fell. Roy. Meteor. Soc.; F.R.A.S.; Fell. Soc. of Tel. Engnr. and Electricians; asst. astronomer, Cambridge, 1848; asst. astronomer, Roy. Observatory, Greenwich, 1854; observer and supt. of telegraphs, S. Australia, 1855; postmr.-gen., supt. of tels., and govt. astronomer, 1870-1901; dcp. postmr.-gen., Austrln. Commonwealth, 1st Mar., 1901; ret., 1905.

TODD, JOHN SPENCER BRIDGES, C.M.G (1878).—B. 1840; jun. clk., col. sec.'s office, Cape, Aug., 1860; 2nd clk. to C.C. and R.M., Swellendam, Dec., 1862; 2nd clk. to C.C.
